To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency-dependent conductivity in ionically conducting glasses can be described by the parallel relaxation model of Almond and co-workers, or, more satisfactorily, by the modified Glarum series relaxation model, which incorporates a diffusion-controlled relaxation mechanism.

the frequency-dependent ac conductivity behaviour of ion-conducting glasses can be described by a model involving parallel relaxation processes, or alternatively, by a model involving series relaxation, and that the latter model, in particular, is more appealing than the former because of the microscopic mechanism of ionic transport which it involves, and because of its simplicity.

the ac conductivity behaviour of ion conducting glasses may be described by a model that is a modification of one originally proposed for the case of polaron transport in amorphou s semiconductors, and that a model originally proposed for the description of dielectric relaxation of molecular liquids may be modified to describe the ac conductivity behaviour, and that the latter model is more intuitive and appealing.

a study of the frequency-dependent (ac conductivity of ionically conducting glass.
a detailed study of ionic transport and dielectric relaxation in glasses.
the development of models for the frequency-dependent conductivity of ionically conducting materials.

the parallel model provides a better description of the data than the serial one, but that both are in qualitative agreement with experiment.
neither the Almond–West nor the Glarum models are able to provide an adequate description of the ac conductivity behaviour of ion conducting glasses.

the frequency-dependent conductivity of ionically conducting amorphous materials may be explained in terms of either a model based on a parallel relaxation process, or a model based on series relaxation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of ionically conducting materials, the frequency-dependent conductivity is best described by the diffusion-controlled relaxation model.
the ac conductivity behaviour of ion conducting glasses can be explained by a combination of the parallel relaxation model and the diffusion-controlled relaxation model.
, while the Almond-West model may be adequate for the interpretation of conductivity data in certain cases, it is not generally applicable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ac conductivity data can be described by either of two models, and that there is no unique model that can describe all the data.

the frequency-dependent ac conductivity of ionically conducting amorphous materials can be accounted for by either parallel or series relaxation processes, depending upon the particular material and the frequency regime of interest.
the frequency-dependent ac conductivity behaviour of ion-conducting glasses is not well described by the Almond–West model.
